name: Run payroll
summary: Every two weeks the payroll team turns approved field time, salaries and HR changes into pay for about 1,350 employees, most of them field staff paid hourly with overtime, day rates, job bonuses and living-out allowances. Six payroll specialists in Calgary receive time released by the district bases, enter new hires, terminations and rate changes, key manual allowances from spreadsheets, check overtime, run and review the calculation, get the controller's approval and send the direct deposit file to the bank. After pay day they answer pay questions, cut off-cycle payments, issue Records of Employment, remit source deductions to the Canada Revenue Agency within three working days and post the payroll journal. Late or wrong field time, rotation overtime rules and constant hiring and layoffs make the work error-prone, and most runs need some off-cycle corrections.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people, roughly 880 of them field staff on rotation or on call at nine district bases, with a Calgary head office for finance, HR, HSE and engineering.
baseline.notes: Biweekly payroll in a vendor HRIS and payroll system fed by field time capture, with manual allowances keyed from district spreadsheets, approval by email and a bank direct deposit file. No automated rules engine for rotation pay; checks are reports and spreadsheets.

trigger: The district bases release approved field time for the two-week pay period to payroll after the period closes.
end_state: Employees are paid by direct deposit on pay day, off-cycle corrections and Records of Employment are issued, source deductions are remitted to CRA and the payroll journal is posted to the general ledger.

volume.seasonality: Runs are fixed at 26 a year (two a month, three in two months of the year). Work per run is higher in December to March and August to November with full crews and hiring, and around spring break-up layoffs and recalls, which add terminations, ROEs and rehires.

evidence.note: Biweekly pay for field and office staff is the common pattern at Canadian service companies; 26 runs a year gives 2.17 a month, matching the organisation file's 2-2.2-3.

surge.cause: Spring break-up layoffs and summer recall, adding terminations, ROEs and rehires to the runs

evidence.note: The number of runs does not change during break-up (multiplier 1.0); the work inside each run rises by an estimated 20-40% because of terminations, ROEs and recalls. Recorded here so a simulation can raise per-run effort, not run counts.

produces.outcome: paid, remitted, posted and register sent for subsidy claim

evidence.note: Six specialists; a little over half their time goes to the two runs a month, the rest to benefits and pension remittances, garnishments, T4 year-end, audits and wage subsidy support. About 90-100 hours of payroll specialist time per run.

roles.title: District administrator (field tickets and job files)

evidence.note: Chasing and correcting late time after it has been released to payroll; the main time compilation sits in crew scheduling. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Entering hires, terminations, recalls and rate changes in the HRIS before each cut-off; about 15-20 changes per run in busy months.
Fixing interface and deduction set-up errors found in the preliminary run.
Approves the payroll register and funding each run.
Releases the payroll funding transfer under dual authorisation. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Reviews and posts the payroll journal; clearing-account reconciliations are done in the month-end close. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: HRIS, field time capture and payroll
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones

steps.name: Load released field time into payroll
steps.description: When the district administrators release the period's approved time, the HRIS imports the hours, travel, standby and bonus codes for each employee into the open pay period and produces an import exception list.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check every district and cost centre has submitted
steps.description: A payroll specialist compares the import report with the list of district bases, service lines and active employees, looks for missing districts, employees with no hours who are on rotation, and codes the import rejected.

error.defect_description: A missing crew is not noticed and its members go unpaid

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Chase late or rejected time
steps.description: The district administrator is phoned or emailed about the missing time, gets the supervisor's daily sheets from location, corrects codes and re-releases the time, sometimes after the cut-off.

error.defect_description: Hours keyed in a hurry with the wrong job or overtime code

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Enter hires, terminations, recalls and rate changes
steps.description: The HR coordinator enters new hire records with SIN, TD1 forms and banking, terminations with last day and reason, recalls after break-up, promotions and pay grid changes in the HRIS before the cut-off.

error.defect_description: Wrong rate, missing banking or a termination entered after the cut-off

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Verify HR changes before they are paid
steps.description: A payroll specialist checks each change against the signed offer, termination form or rate letter, confirms banking and tax forms, and sends back anything that does not match. HR enters, payroll verifies.

control.basis: Internal control over payroll: the person who sets up employees and rates is not the person who approves them for pay

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Key manual allowances and job bonuses
steps.description: Payroll specialists key living-out allowances, subsistence, job and stage bonuses, safety bonuses and retention payments from district spreadsheets that the time capture screens cannot hold, each specialist taking a group of districts.

error.defect_description: Bonus keyed to the wrong employee or twice

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check overtime, statutory holiday and rotation pay
steps.description: Payroll specialists run reports of daily and weekly hours, compare overtime paid with the daily and weekly thresholds and any averaging agreements, add general holiday pay and flag employees whose hours look impossible for their rotation.

control.basis: Alberta Employment Standards Code: overtime, averaging agreements and general holiday pay; BC Employment Standards Act for BC-based staff

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Run preliminary payroll calculation
steps.description: The payroll system calculates gross pay, CPP, EI, income tax, benefits and garnishment deductions and net pay for every employee and produces the preliminary register and variance reports.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review preliminary register and variances
steps.description: A senior payroll specialist compares gross pay by district and cost centre with the last run, and scans for negative or zero nets, unusually large cheques, employees paid twice and new hires with no banking.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Correct pay errors
steps.description: The specialist corrects the hours, earnings or deduction lines found in review, documents each correction and asks for the calculation to be run again.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Fix interface or deduction set-up
steps.description: The HRIS analyst traces why an import, benefit deduction or tax set-up produced wrong results, fixes the configuration or mapping and tells payroll when the run can be repeated.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Prepare payroll summary and funding request
steps.description: The senior specialist prints the final register totals, net pay, employer and employee source deductions and the change from the last run, and writes the funding request with the amount and value date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Approve payroll register and funding
steps.description: The controller reviews the summary against the last run and the headcount, asks about large changes and approves the register and funding by email or signature.

control.basis: Payroll approval by someone outside the payroll team before funds are released (internal control over financial reporting)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Release payroll funding
steps.description: The treasury manager sets up the transfer of net pay to the payroll account in the bank portal and a second signer releases it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Transmit direct deposit file and publish pay statements
steps.description: The payroll specialist finalises the run, sends the direct deposit file to the bank at least two banking days before pay day and publishes electronic pay statements with hours, rates, earnings and deductions.

control.basis: Alberta Employment Standards: pay within 10 consecutive days after the end of the pay period and a statement of earnings each pay period

evidence.note: Pay due within 10 days of the period end and statements required each period (src2); timing of the file estimated.

steps.name: Bank settles deposits on pay day
steps.description: The bank processes the direct deposit file overnight on its settlement cycle and the net pay reaches each employee's own bank account on the morning of pay day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Answer pay queries from field staff
steps.description: Payroll specialists answer calls and emails from employees and supervisors about missing hours, overtime, bonuses and deductions, look up the time and earnings and decide whether an off-cycle payment is owed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Process off-cycle payments
steps.description: For missed hours, missed bonuses and final pay the specialist enters an off-cycle run or manual cheque, gets it approved by the payroll lead and sends the deposit.

error.defect_description: Off-cycle payment duplicates an amount already in the next regular run

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Issue Records of Employment
steps.description: For each employee who left or was laid off in the period the specialist completes the electronic Record of Employment with insurable hours and earnings and the reason code and submits it to Service Canada.

control.basis: Employment Insurance Regulations: electronic ROE within 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period with the interruption of earnings

evidence.note: Five-day ROE deadline for biweekly pay periods (src3); about 10-25 departures per run estimated from 25-35% annual turnover.

steps.name: Remit source deductions to CRA
steps.description: The specialist totals income tax, CPP and EI withheld plus the employer share for the remitting period and pays it through the bank to the Canada Revenue Agency by the third working day after the period ends.

control.basis: Income Tax Act and CRA remitting rules for accelerated threshold 2 remitters

evidence.note: Threshold 2 remitters (average monthly withholding of $100,000 or more) pay up to four times a month, three working days after each period (src1); a 1,350-person payroll of about $130-170 million a year is well above that threshold.

steps.name: Review and post payroll journal
steps.description: An accountant reviews the payroll journal produced by the interface, checks that debits by cost centre and service line equal net pay, deductions and accruals, and posts it to the ledger.

error.defect_description: Journal posted to the wrong cost centre

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Send payroll register for the wage subsidy claim
steps.description: During the CEWS period the specialist exports the register with eligible remuneration by employee and week and sends it to the accountant preparing the wage subsidy claim.

next.outcome: paid, remitted, posted and register sent for subsidy claim

evidence.note: CEWS was credited against personnel expenses in 2021 (src4); share of runs (about 17 of 48 months) estimated.

exceptions.name: Late field time
exceptions.description: One or more districts release time late or with rejected codes and payroll chases it before the cut-off.

exceptions.name: Off-cycle corrections
exceptions.description: Missed hours, bonuses or final pay are paid in an off-cycle run after pay day.

exceptions.name: System set-up fault
exceptions.description: A deduction, tax or interface set-up error forces the HRIS analyst to fix the configuration and the calculation to be repeated.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from approved field time reaching payroll to remittance and journal posted
benchmarks.population: Biweekly payroll at a Canadian oilfield service company, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Estimate: time arrives two to three days after the period ends; pay must be within 10 days of the period end (src2) and remittance within three working days of the weekly remitting period (src1), so pay day falls about 6-8 days after time arrives and remittance and posting two to five days later.

pain_points.description: Districts release time late or with wrong codes, so payroll chases supervisors on remote locations near the cut-off.

evidence.note: Organisation file description of late or wrong field time; author's estimate of frequency.

pain_points.description: Allowances and job bonuses are keyed by hand from spreadsheets because the time capture cannot hold them, which causes most pay errors.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Most runs end with off-cycle payments and queries from field staff, adding a third of a run's work after pay day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Hiring waves and break-up layoffs add many set-ups, terminations and ROEs with short legal deadlines.

evidence.note: ROE deadline (src3); difficulty attracting and retaining field personnel (src4).

sources.title: When to remit (pay) source deductions: remitter types and due dates
sources.supports: Remitter types set by average monthly withholding two years earlier; accelerated threshold 2 (AMWA of $100,000 or more) remits up to four times a month for the periods ending on the 7th, 14th, 21st and month-end, each due on the third working day after the period ends.

sources.title: Payment of earnings
sources.supports: Pay periods may be weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly or monthly; regular pay is due within 10 consecutive days after the end of the pay period; a statement of earnings with hours, rates, earnings and deductions is required each pay period; termination pay within 10 days after the pay period end or 31 days after the last day of employment; records kept 3 years.

sources.title: How to complete the Record of Employment form
sources.supports: For weekly, biweekly and semi-monthly pay periods an electronic ROE is due no later than 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period in which the interruption of earnings occurs.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Three Tier 4 DGB fleets (126,000 HHP) operating at end 2022; fourth fleet (42,000 HHP) field ready by end Q1 2023 and fifth approved for early 2024; upgrades include 3,000 HHP continuous duty pumps and idle reduction packages; fully electric sand, blending and chemical equipment developed; capital spending $103.6 million in 2022 mainly Tier 4 upgrades; supply chain challenges such as long lead times on key parts; record inflation; difficulty adding field crews and attracting and retaining qualified personnel; recruiting events; CEWS credited against personnel expenses in 2021 ($10.2 million in cost of sales); the company has safety and training programs; MD&A dated February 22, 2023.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).
The case starts when approved time reaches payroll; compiling and approving field time belongs to fo-dist-crew-scheduling-and-rotation and is not repeated here.
Cadence is recorded as 'weekly' because the format has no biweekly option; runs are every two weeks (2.17 a month).
The organisation file lists payroll-specialist, hris-analyst, controller and hr-coordinator; district-admin (late time), treasury-ir-manager (funding release) and accountant (journal) also take part.
Off-cycle runs are part of the regular run they correct rather than separate cases.
Benefit carrier, pension and garnishment remittances, T4 year-end and wage subsidy claim preparation are outside this workflow.

The simulated median (about 12 days) runs slightly above the 10-day benchmark because it includes the remittance calendar wait and journal posting after pay day; pay day itself falls about 7 days after time arrives, inside the Alberta 10-day limit.
Stated FTE (about 4.9) is roughly twice the hands-on time per run because payroll specialists' time between runs also goes to queries, audits, set-up and reporting that are not modelled step by step.
